primary_claim: Adding an SAE loss term as a regularizer during LLM training (jointly training SAE layers alongside model weights) improves downstream SAE feature sparsity/reconstruction quality on nearly all layers of a small character-level GPT-2 model, without apparently harming overall model performance.

effect.metric: cross-entropy loss increase at fixed SAE sparsity (L0~50)
effect.value: SAE regularization reliably yields better (lower) cross-entropy loss increase on most layers; less dependable on some layers (e.g. layer 3); regularized models also reach slightly lower overall cross-entropy loss

stated_future_work: explore alternative approaches that yield more reliable improvements or computationally efficient implementations
try SAE regularization on a more capable model such as GPT-2 small, which may require fine-tuning rather than training from scratch
limitations_stated: studied only on a toy model that easily overfits the small Shakespeare dataset; results may differ on larger models/datasets
regularization coefficients were chosen to amplify the effect and smaller coefficients haven't been studied
further technical advancements likely needed before this applies to interpreting frontier models
quote: We find that SAE regularization improves SAE performance on all layers and does not seem to impact the model's overall performance.
